title: ABS Wheel Speed Sensor Fault
shortDescription: ABS module reports wheel speed sensor fault.
fullDescription:
BMW Motorrad fault 18002 indicates a wheel speed sensor failure detected by integral ABS. ABS will disable and dash shows ABS warning.

Common from dirt accumulation on sensor tip or damaged tone ring.

fixSteps.title: Check air gap
fixSteps.instruction: ~1 mm between sensor and tone ring.

faq.q: Can I ride with ABS off?

title: CAN Bus Communication Fault
shortDescription: Loss of CAN communication between modules.
fullDescription:
Fault 22001 on BMW Motorrad indicates CAN bus disruption. May affect dash, ABS, ASC and engine management simultaneously.

Causes include corroded connectors, aftermarket accessory with poor CAN integration, or failed module.

fixSteps.title: Remove accessories
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug non-OEM CAN devices and retest.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Clean multi-pin plugs at ECU and DWA modules.

fixSteps.title: Dealer scan
fixSteps.instruction: GS-911 or BMW MOSS diagnosis of CAN health.

whenToCallPro: Intermittent CAN issues need pro tools.

faq.a: Very helpful — affordable home alternative to MOSS.

title: Fuel Pump Control Fault
shortDescription: Fuel pump not reaching target pressure.
fullDescription:
35002 indicates ECU commands fuel pump but rail pressure low. Bike may not start or cut out at high throttle.

Common with aging in-tank pumps on high-mileage GS/RT.

fixSteps.title: Check fuel pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Should be 3.5-5 bar depending on model.

title: EWS Immobilizer Fault
fullDescription:
Fault 36002 means engine ECU did not receive valid handshake from EWS/Ring antenna. Bike will not start.

Causes: dying key battery, faulty ring antenna around ignition, or EWS module issue.

fixSteps.title: Try spare key
fixSteps.instruction: Use backup key to confirm key issue.

fixSteps.title: Replace antenna
fixSteps.instruction: Ring around ignition can be unplugged and swapped.

faq.a: Most BMW keys don't have battery — chip is passive.

title: Throttle Body Fault
fullDescription:
Fault 42001 indicates electronic throttle position disagreement between primary and secondary sensor. Bike enters fail-safe with reduced throttle.

Common after butterfly cleaning without TPS calibration via GS-911.

faq.a: For BMW owners, yes — covers many adaptations.

title: O2 Lambda Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Oxygen sensor signal out of range.
fullDescription:
Fault 28002 indicates lambda sensor signal fault. BMW uses Bosch wideband on most modern models.

Aftermarket exhaust without correct bung often triggers this.

faq.a: OEM — wideband is tuned to ECU.

title: Injector Circuit Fault
fullDescription:
30001 reports injector circuit issue. Twin or inline engines will miss on affected cylinder.

Check harness connector first — vibration can loosen on GS models.

faq.a: Yes — can actuate injectors for testing.

title: Battery Voltage Low
fullDescription:
10000 indicates ECU sees under-voltage. BMW AGM batteries can drop capacity suddenly; combined with parasitic drain this code appears.

Replace battery or fix charging system.

fixSteps.title: Battery test
fixSteps.instruction: Load test and measure charging voltage.

fixSteps.title: Replace battery
fixSteps.instruction: Install AGM type 12V, size per spec.

title: Camshaft Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
40001 indicates cam sensor fault. On BMW boxers mounted at valve cover area; prone to oil contamination.

On inline-four K and S models mounted near timing chain cover.

faq.a: Valve cover gasket often needs replacement too.

title: Ignition Coil Fault
shortDescription: Coil primary circuit open or shorted.
fullDescription:
38001 indicates coil primary fault. BMW inline-fours use coil-on-plug; boxers use remote coils.

Replace coil, verify spark and plug condition.

fixSteps.title: Inspect coil
fixSteps.instruction: Check for cracks, swap with known good.

title: ESA Suspension Fault
fullDescription:
24001 appears on ESA-equipped BMW when suspension actuator can't reach commanded setting. Stepper motor or shock sensor failure.

ESA disables and suspension reverts to a fixed mode.

fixSteps.title: Replace actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Some actuators swap separately; shock rebuild may be needed.

whenToCallPro: ESA shock rebuild is specialist work.

faq.a: Warning remains but bike rides on manual setting.

title: ABS Pump Motor Fault
shortDescription: Integral ABS pump motor not running.
fullDescription:
18003 indicates ABS pump motor did not complete its self-test. Older servo-assist models (K1200LT, R1150RT) particularly affected.

Motor brushes and internal seals can degrade requiring ABS unit rebuild.

faq.a: Brakes still work but without ABS — use caution.
